question: Are there any red flags in Apple's financial statements?

answer.summary: Apple's FY2023 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2023) carries several pre-computed red flags, though none are severe: the current ratio was below 1.0 in both FY2022 (0.88) and FY2023 (0.99) [F01420][F01421], and FY2023 inventory grew 28% while cost of revenue fell 4% [F00099][F00022]. Operating cash flow declined 9.5% to $110.54B and free cash flow fell 10.6% to $99.58B in FY2023 [F00224][F01389]. Revenue fell 2.8% to $383.29B and operating income fell 4.3% to $114.30B [F00013][F00037], while interest coverage dropped 29% from 40.7x to 29.1x [F01432]. Shareholder payouts (dividends plus buybacks) of $92.58B consumed 93% of free cash flow in FY2023 [F01448][F01389]. The auditor issued an unqualified opinion dated November 2, 2023 [T00627], and all 3 accounting identities passed with no text-vs-table conflicts, so these are watch items rather than confirmed problems.

key_numbers.metric: Inventory growth vs cost of revenue
Net cash provided by operating activities
Dividends + buybacks as % of free cash flow

drivers: FY2023 free cash flow decline (-10.6%, $111.44B -> $99.58B) coincides with the 9.5% operating cash flow decline ($122.15B -> $110.54B) while capex was roughly flat at $10.96B (+2.3% YoY), so the FCF movement is driven by operating cash flow, not capital spending [F01389][F00224][F00236].

Component-level attribution of the FY2023 revenue decline (-2.8%, $394.33B -> $383.29B) is not in the retrieved evidence; no ATTRIBUTION block was provided for the revenue or operating income lines [F00013][F00037].
risks_and_red_flags: Liquidity: current ratio below 1.0 in FY2022 (0.88) and FY2023 (0.99) [F01420][F01421].
Inventory build-up: FY2023 inventory grew 28% while cost of revenue fell 4% (collection / build-up risk) [F00099][F00022].
Operating cash flow decline: FY2023 OCF fell 9.5% ($122.15B -> $110.54B) [F00224].
Payout strain: FY2022 dividends+buybacks of $104.24B were 94% of free cash flow ($111.44B) [F01447][F01388].
Payout strain: FY2023 dividends+buybacks of $92.58B were 93% of free cash flow ($99.58B), leaving little room to absorb a downturn [F01448][F01389].
Operating income decline: FY2023 operating income fell 4.3% ($119.44B -> $114.30B) [F00037].
Interest coverage drop: FY2023 interest coverage fell 29% (40.7x -> 29.1x) [F01432].
data_quality_notes: 3 accounting identities passed, 0 failed for the screened numbers; no text-vs-table conflicts reported.
The red-flag screen (current ratio <1, payout ratios, coverage) is a pre-computed analytical screen, not an auditor finding; the auditor's report is unqualified [T00627].
Free cash flow is a derived metric (CFO - Capex), already computed in the evidence; it is not an XBRL-tagged line [F01389].

outlook.actuals_view: FY2023 actuals show broad but modest declines: revenue -2.8%, operating income -4.3%, operating cash flow -9.5%, free cash flow -10.6%, and interest coverage down 29%, alongside a sub-1.0 current ratio and a 28% inventory build against falling cost of revenue [F00013][F00037][F00224][F01389][F01432][F01421][F00099].
outlook.forward_looking_guidance: not in the retrieved evidence (no management guidance facts were provided).

follow_up_checks: Determine whether the FY2023 inventory build (+28% vs cost of revenue -4%) reflects a product transition/launch timing or demand softness [F00099][F00022].
Identify the current-liability composition driving the sub-1.0 current ratio (e.g., commercial paper) and confirm liquidity is supported by cash and investments [F01420][F01421].
Assess sustainability of returning 93-94% of free cash flow via dividends and buybacks if FCF declines further [F01447][F01448].
Verify what drove the 29% interest coverage drop - higher interest expense versus lower operating income [F01432][F00037].
Obtain segment/product-line revenue detail to attribute the 2.8% FY2023 revenue decline, which is not broken out in the retrieved evidence [F00013].
